title: Who's Behind the Text? Robust Model Authorship Attribution
abstract: arXiv:2610.19583v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate text, their misuse has become a growing societal problem, with implications for academic misconduct, model distillation, and cyberattacks. For these reasons, Model Authorship Attribution (MAA), which identifies the source model of a given text, is important for promoting the responsible use of LLMs and improving AI safety. In practice, attribution systems must remain reliable beyond the distributions observed during training. They may encounter texts from unseen domains and writing settings, as well as generations from future versions of model families that were not available when the system was trained. However, existing MAA methods often exhibit substantial performance degradation under such distribution shifts. translated_title: 文本背后是谁？鲁棒的模型作者归属
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型越来越多地被用于生成文本，其滥用已成为一个日益严重的社会问题，涉及学术不端、模型蒸馏和网络攻击等方面。因此，模型作者归属（MAA）——即识别给定文本的来源模型——对于促进大语言模型的负责任使用和提升人工智能安全具有重要意义。在实际应用中，归属系统必须在训练时观察到的分布之外仍然保持可靠，它们可能会遇到来自未见过的领域和写作场景的文本，以及来自系统训练时尚不存在的模型家族未来版本所生成的文本。然而，现有的MAA方法在这种分布偏移下往往会出现显著的性能下降。为应对这一挑战，我们提出了一种基于似然的来源归属作者追踪方法ATLAS，它通过以来源为条件的……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出基于似然的模型作者归属方法ATLAS，能够在未见领域、未知写作场景以及模型家族未来版本等分布偏移下依然稳健地识别文本的来源大语言模型。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes ATLAS, a likelihood-based Model Authorship Attribution method that robustly identifies the source LLM behind a given text even under distribution shifts such as unseen domains, writing settings, and future versions of model families.
